posts.content_md:
Hi everybody. It is a long time ago that i write something in English but i give a try.

David ( holomaker ) sell very interesting lasers from laser pico projectors. I search for it on the internet and looks that the pico laser engine is a

very interesting module to make color holograms. 

I order one on the internet.

The green laser is good to make holograms but the red and blue i don't know. I am not sure if it is mode hopping you have to play with the current and temperature.

First when i receive the projector i will remove one mirror out of the projector then the white laserbeam will pass the scanner. That means i have a perfect alignt laserbeam. I connect the projector to a I phone and i will send a white screen to the projector that means that the laser beam willbe white.

If i want to controll the current for the red and blue diode I will send another color to the projector. The temperature controll is more tricky

Look at this link for the construction off the laser engine.

[https://www.experimental-engineering.co ... projector/](https://www.experimental-engineering.co.uk/microvision-showwx-hdmi-laser-pico-projector/)

If it doesnt work to make holograms with it then it is a perfect light to illuminate a hologram.

I am very curious if it works. you have perfect color control to make a color hologram. I let you know the results.

posts.post_subject: Laser pico projector for making color holograms
posts.content_md: The pico engine was modified heavily: Red and Blue diode was removed and turned 90deg to have same polarisation as Green. Added TEC, thermistor and shutters. Created specialized quad high stable, low noise drivers for laser diodes and PPLN heater, an Arduino based TEC and shutter controllers. Exact wavelenghts are 449.1, 528.4 and 640.7nm. Created FPSI and tuned the diodes and OPSL to SLM. Later I will add monitor photodiodes to monitor noise...

posts.topic_title: Laser pico projector for making color holograms
posts.author: soda
posts.post_subject: Laser pico projector for making color holograms
posts.content_md: The shutter actuators are made from relays ) with soldered Cu foil arms which block the beams. The green OPSL module needs current drivers, I use 406.5 mA for the IR diode and 81mA for PPLN heater, which is really sensitive. I need to set temperature around 22C, due to the red diode at low temperatures is multimode. Note the prism, which reflect sample beam to FPSI - unfortuntely needs to be tuned constantly. The green OPSL wants to be cooler and red warmer to stay single mode and diodes are really sensitive to backreflections from spatial filter and FPSI...

posts.content_md:
Hello,

I finally managed to have a first look at those neat devices and do some measurements, thanks David for sending a couple. Now the first thing was to kill the red diode of one device. I like to replace it, but it is totally unclear whether it is practically feasible, given the ultra-precise but hardly adjustable press-mount. 

So the question is: did anybody succeed replacing the red diode without messing up beam collimation and centering?

An analogous question is about the PL530. As it turns out, they can vary quite a lot in power and spectral purity. On the other hand, the collimation optics of the white light engine is pretty good. However, the PL530 seems pretty tightly pressed into the holder, and it is unclear whether it makes sense to try to replace it with a better one. 

So the question is: did anybody succeed with replacing the PL530 while maintaining the excellent collimation?

Thanks for tips!

Wolfgang
